title.narrative: Increased capacity of constituents to develop fair and effective labour migration laws, frameworks, institutions and services to protect migrant workers

description.narrative: Myanmar has faced significant political upheaval since the military takeover on February 1, 2021, leading to a humanitarian crisis and widespread human rights violations. This turmoil has resulted in approximately 3.5 million internally displaced people by the end of 2024 and 19.9 million requiring humanitarian assistance, affecting one-third of the population. As a result of expanding armed conflicts, severe natural disaster, disease outbreaks, and economic and political instability, people fled/migrate to neighbouring countries or resettled in third countries. Myanmar witnesses international migration and internal migration surged. ILO plays a significant role in supporting migrant workers through various initiative. One of the most efficient initiatives is the establishment of Migrant Resource Centres (MRC) around the country as well as near border towns. Through ILO support, MRC provide fair recruitment guideline by disseminating information pamphlet, peer to peer discussion. The Myanmar Domestic Workers Association was established in February 2023 with an initial group of 21 domestic workers. The association expanded to 350 members now joining. ILO supporting to the association include strengthening the association membership and equipping them with soft skills which include social dialogue and promotion of compliance with ILO Conventions 189.
